Maintenance Report — MNT-0065-002

Asset: WELL-0065 (SW-24 Well 065, T350, Southwest Block 24) Equipment: flowline Work started: 04 Feb 2023 08:00 · Finished: 07 Feb 2023 02:00 · Well stopped for this job: 66 hours Crew lead: Kevin Price (U-303) · Crew: Daniel Foster Triggered by: inspection INS-0065-0016 on 2023-02-02 Report written: 08 Feb 2023

What happened

Field staff reported that a damp, dark patch appeared along the flowline route. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0065-0016 showed the wellhead at 19.3 °C with the air at 11.8 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. Excavation found a corrosion pinhole on the bottom of the line.

Root cause

External corrosion where the pipe coating had been damaged.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 6 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).
  • Hot work permit issued for welding; gas test before welding read 1% LEL, below the 10% limit (WS-04).

Work done

  1. Excavated around the leak.
  2. Cut out the corroded section.
  3. Welded in a new section of line pipe.
  4. Coated the new joint.
  5. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: cut out and replaced the corroded flowline section.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 360 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 288 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Waste

  • Oily soil from the excavation and the cut-out pipe sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0065-002 (WS-06).

Maintenance Report — MNT-0065-015

Asset: WELL-0065 (SW-24 Well 065, T350, Southwest Block 24) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 07 Mar 2025 08:00 · Finished: 26 Mar 2025 19:00 · Well stopped for this job: 467 hours Crew lead: Kevin Price (U-303) · Crew: Brian Coleman · Contractor: Coyote Ridge Well Services Triggered by: inspection INS-0065-0121 on 2025-03-06 Report written: 28 Mar 2025

What happened

Field staff reported that the motor breaker kept tripping and the pump jack would not run. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0065-0121 showed the wellhead at 21.8 °C with the air at 14.7 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. An insulation test showed a winding fault, so the motor was replaced with an exchange unit. The well stayed shut in for about 17 days longer than the repair itself because the replacement part was back-ordered from the supplier.

Root cause

Moisture got into the motor terminal box and damaged the windings.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 5 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Disconnected and removed the motor.
  2. Fitted the exchange motor on the existing base.
  3. Aligned the sheaves and tensioned the belts.
  4. Checked rotation direction and motor current.

Summary of the fix: replaced the electric motor with an exchange unit.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 2 hours; motor current within the nameplate rating and stroke rate normal. The well was returned to production.

maintenance.action: Fished and replaced parted rod section
maintenance.report_html:
Maintenance Report — MNT-0065-025

Asset: WELL-0065 (SW-24 Well 065, T350, Southwest Block 24) Equipment: rod string Work started: 09 May 2026 08:00 · Finished: 19 May 2026 03:00 · Well stopped for this job: 235 hours Crew lead: Daniel Foster (U-302) · Crew: Megan Ward Triggered by: inspection INS-0065-0181 on 2026-05-07 Report written: 20 May 2026

What happened

Field staff reported that the operator noticed the pump jack running unusually light and no fluid reaching the flowline. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0065-0181 showed the wellhead at 34.8 °C with the air at 28.2 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. A dynamometer card showed no load from the downhole pump, which points to a parted rod. The company workover rig was busy on other wells, so the well waited about 8 days for it; the work itself took about 2 days.

Root cause

A coupling unscrewed after repeated rod buckling at the bottom of the stroke.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Rigged up the company workover rig on the well.
  2. Pulled the rod string and located the break.
  3. Recovered the lower section with an overshot fishing tool.
  4. Replaced the damaged rods.
  5. Ran the rod string back in and spaced out the pump.

Summary of the fix: fished and replaced parted rod section.

Testing and return to service

Pump test showed normal fluid delivery and the rod load returned to normal. The well was returned to production.

Maintenance Report — MNT-0065-026

Asset: WELL-0065 (SW-24 Well 065, T350, Southwest Block 24) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 23 May 2026 08:00 · Finished: 02 Jun 2026 12:00 · Well stopped for this job: 244 hours Crew lead: Daniel Foster (U-302) · Crew: Brian Coleman · Contractor: Coyote Ridge Well Services Triggered by: inspection INS-0065-0183 on 2026-05-21 Report written: 02 Jun 2026

What happened

Field staff reported that the pump jack was running rough with a loud knock at the top of each stroke, so the operator stopped it. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0065-0183 showed the wellhead at 33.0 °C with the air at 27.0 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. A vibration check and visual inspection found play in the saddle bearing and scoring on the bearing housing. The well stayed shut in for about 8 days longer than the repair itself because the replacement part was back-ordered from the supplier.

Root cause

Bearing wear from long service and an overdue grease interval.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Lowered the horsehead and supported the walking beam with a crane.
  2. Removed the saddle bearing assembly.
  3. Cleaned the housing and checked alignment.
  4. Fitted a new saddle bearing and torqued the bolts to the manufacturer's values.
  5. Greased all structural bearings.

Summary of the fix: replaced saddle bearing and re-greased.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 2 hours: smooth stroke, no knocking, bearing temperature normal. The well was returned to production.

ItemUSD
Saddle bearing assembly1,023
Bolts, shims and seals256
Bearing grease and consumables426
Labour (company crew and contractor)1,051
Total2,756

Notes and recommendations

  • Shorten the grease interval on this unit to 60 days.
  • Check saddle bearings on neighbouring units of the same age.
